steps.title: Download PPMI miRNA dataset
steps.instruction: Access the PPMI database via the LONI archive (www.ppmi-info.org) using an approved account and signed data‑usage agreement; download blood‑derived miRNA expression profiles for the Clinical PD, Prodromal PD, and SWEDD cohorts. Verify that all samples are properly annotated and free of missing or inconsistent data before proceeding.

steps.title: Verify dataset integrity
steps.instruction: Extract the downloaded files and confirm that all expected files are present and complete.

steps.title: Install R and DESeq2
steps.instruction: Install R version ≥ 4.1.0 and the latest stable DESeq2 package (compatible with the installed R version). Estimated time: 1 h.

substeps.instruction: Linux with root: sudo apt update && sudo apt install r-base
Linux without root: conda create -n r_env r-base=4.1.0 && conda activate r_env
Windows: download the installer from https://cran.r-project.org and run it
macOS: download the binary from https://cran.r-project.org, double‑click and install
In R, run install.packages("DESeq2") (or BiocManager::install("DESeq2") if needed)

steps.title: Install Python and pyMaBoSS
steps.instruction: Install Python version ≥ 3.8 and pyMaBoSS version ≥ 2.0. Estimated time: 1 h.

substeps.instruction: Linux with root: sudo apt update && sudo apt install python
Linux (recommended) – Conda: conda create -n my_python_env python=3.8 && conda activate my_python_env
Linux (recommended) – Mamba: mamba create -n my_python_env python=3.8 && mamba activate my_python_env
Windows: download the installer from https://www.python.org, run it and check “Add Python to PATH”
macOS: install Python 3.8 via Homebrew, then create a Conda/Mamba environment
Install pyMaBoSS: pip install pyMaBoSS
Verify installation: python -m maboss --version

steps.title: Install CellDesigner and access MINERVA
steps.instruction: Download CellDesigner 4 from celldesigner.org and install a 4.x version compatible with SBML‑qual. Access the MINERVA platform and ensure the MINERVA plugin is available. Verify software compatibility: R ≥ 4.1.0, DESeq2 latest stable; Python ≥ 3.8, pyMaBoSS ≥ 2.0; CellDesigner 4.x; MINERVA plugin; CaSQ version ≥ 1.0.3.

steps.title: Load R libraries
steps.instruction: Start R, install DESeq2 if missing via BiocManager::install("DESeq2"), then load the required libraries with library(DESeq2) and library(readr).

steps.title: Import miRNA count matrix and metadata
steps.instruction: Read the raw miRNA count matrix and sample metadata (CSV files) using readr functions. Ensure the matrix follows Table 1 format (rows = miRNA_ID, columns = samples with raw read counts) and the metadata follows Table 2 format (sample_ID, Condition, Sex). Replace file‑path placeholders with the actual locations of your files.

steps.title: Filter miRNAs by significance
steps.instruction: Apply filtering thresholds: adjusted p‑value < 0.05 and absolute log2 fold change > 1.5. Save the filtered list to filtered_miRNAs.csv with write.csv(as.data.frame(res), file = "filtered_miRNAs.csv"). CRITICAL: Apply these thresholds consistently to maintain reproducibility.

steps.title: Perform MINERVA pathway enrichment
steps.instruction: Connect to the MINERVA platform using the minervar package, retrieve map components and annotation types for a public project such as the Parkinson’s Disease Map, and save enrichment results. Then convert the retrieved SBML file to a PNG image for visualization. Estimated time: 2–3 h.

substeps.instruction: Load library(minervar)
Define MINERVA API URL and project ID (e.g., Parkinson’s Disease Map)
Retrieve map components and annotation types
Save enrichment results to pathway_enrichment_results.csv
Set file_path <- system.file("extdata", "core.xml", package = "minervar")
If file exists, run convert_to_image(source_file_path = file_path, source_format = "CellDesigner_SBML", target_format = "png")
Save the image as pathway_visualization.png and open it with browseURL
Select an appropriate annotation type (HGNC_SYMBOL, UNIPROT, or ENTREZ) before conversion

steps.title: Parameterize Boolean models
steps.instruction: Using the cohort‑specific omics data obtained in Step 1, determine each miRNA’s regulatory direction based on its expression level and assign probabilities to miRNA‑target interactions using CLES values (higher miRNA expression → stronger target inhibition; lower expression → weaker inhibition).

steps.title: Calibrate Boolean model initial states
steps.instruction: Set the initial state of each target molecule according to the probabilities derived from miRNA expression data, and verify that all Boolean functions correctly reflect the identified pathways.

steps.title: Run simulations and identify modules
steps.instruction: Execute simulations with GINsim12 and BoolNet to explore steady‑states and dynamic behaviors of key pathways. Identify regulatory modules as groups of molecules whose activity patterns differ significantly between cohorts, and compare attractor states across cohorts to characterize module behavior.

steps.title: Conduct sensitivity analysis
steps.instruction: Assess the impact of each molecule on pathway dynamics using the Rmut package for knockout and overexpression perturbations, and perform Monte Carlo simulations in MaBoSS to estimate confidence intervals of model predictions. Estimated time: 6–8 h.
